title: Two Pawns on One File
setup: Black gave up the dark-squared bishop to double White's c-pawns, and White has just snatched a pawn on c5. Attack both c-pawns at once.
hint: White's c-pawns stand on c3 and c5, one file and no pawn to guard either. Find the square that looks at both at once.
explanation:
## The Idea

The bishop was traded for a knight so that White's c-pawns would end up stacked. Here they cost something.

{{Qa5}} attacks both: c3 along the diagonal and c5 along the fifth rank, and no white pawn can defend either one. If White props up c3 with {{Bd2}}, {{Qxc5}} takes the pawn back. White's best is to push the e-pawn first and drive your knight off d5.

Material comes out level, but the doubled pawns stay. Attack the weakness a pawn cannot defend.
